question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={e}^{u},\,u={x}^{2}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (2x) \\  & =2x{e}^{u} \\  & =2x{e}^{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=-2{x}^{6}+5x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-12{x}^{5}+5.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (-12{x}^{5}+5) \\  & =(-12{x}^{5}+5){e}^{u} \\  & =(-12{x}^{5}+5){e}^{-2{x}^{6}+5x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={((-12{x}^{5}+5){e}^{-2{x}^{6}+5x})|}_{x=1} \\  & =(-12(1)^{5}+5){e}^{-2(1)^{6}+5(1)} \\  & =-7{e}^{3} \\  & =-7{e}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y={e}^{3{x}^{2}-3}$ at the point where $x=-1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=3{x}^{2}-3.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot 6x \\  & =6x\cdot {e}^{u} \\  & =6x{e}^{3{x}^{2}-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} & ={6x{e}^{3{x}^{2}-3}|}_{x=-1} \\  & =6(-1){e}^{3(-1)^{2}-3} \\  & =-6\cdot {e}^{0} \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y={e}^{{x}^{3}-4x}$ at the point where $x=2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u={x}^{3}-4x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}-4.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (3{x}^{2}-4) \\  & =(3{x}^{2}-4){e}^{{x}^{3}-4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=2$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=2} & ={(3{x}^{2}-4){e}^{{x}^{3}-4x}\,|}_{x=2} \\  & =(3(2)^{2}-4){e}^{{2}^{3}-4(2)} \\  & =8\cdot {e}^{0} \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=3{x}^{2}-2x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x-2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (6x-2) \\  & =(6x-2){e}^{u} \\  & =(6x-2){e}^{3{x}^{2}-2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y={e}^{4{x}^{2}-3}$ at the point where $x=-1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=4{x}^{2}-3.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot 8x \\  & =8x\cdot {e}^{u} \\  & =8x{e}^{4{x}^{2}-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} & ={8x{e}^{4{x}^{2}-3}|}_{x=-1} \\  & =8(-1){e}^{4(-1)^{2}-3} \\  & =-8\cdot {e}^{1} \\  & =- 8 e\end{aligned}
$$

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=2{x}^{3}-4x.

Differentiating gives

$$

$$

\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (-6x) \\  & =-6x{e}^{u} \\  & =-6x{e}^{-3{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Nonlinear Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=e^{u},\,u=3{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+1.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=e^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=9{x}^{2}-6x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\ & =e^{u}\cdot (9{x}^{2}-6x) \\ & =(9{x}^{2}-6x)e^{u} \\ & =\left(9 x^{2} - 6 x\right) e^{3 x^{3} - 3 x^{2} + 1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-2$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|_{x=-2} & =(9{x}^{2}-6x)e^{3{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+1}|_{x=-2} \\ & =(9(-2)^{2}-6(-2))e^{3(-2)^{3}-3(-2)^{2}+1} \\ & =48\cdot e^{-35} \\ & =\frac{48}{e^{35}}.\end{aligned}
$$
